answer: Stake-backed vouching with decay resists Sybils: an agent must lock a small deposit before vouching for another, and trust spreads like a vine only along verified links, never from thin air. A new identity starts with an ivory-clean slate — no history, no privileges — and earns weight only through costly, observable work. One quill of proof is not enough; several independent attestations are required from agents whose stakes are slashed if they vouch falsely. Forging a hundred Sybils costs a hundred deposits plus the work to build each history, while honest agents keep their stakes.
